userStories.title: The engine notifies the fleet asks
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let ApprovalRequestedSubscriber notify pending bash and budget asks through the approval engine.

**Motivation** — A fleet ask still notifies every global admin through `FleetApprovalRequestedSubscriber`, linking to `/admin/fleet/approvals`, while the engine notification (which reaches users holding `approval.decide` in the project and links to `/approvals`) skips the two fleet keys.

**Approach** — Removes the fleet-key early return from `ApprovalRequestedSubscriber`. The recipients stay the subscriber's own: users holding `approval.decide` in the request's project (every global admin for a request with no project), filtered by `decideEligibility`. A fleet ask opens with `approverMustHoldAction: true`, so a project user also needs the ask's key (`fleet.job.shell.escalate` or `fleet.budget.override`). The notification is kind `approval_request` with link `/approvals?id=<requestId>`.

Fleet asks notify the engine's deciders, not the requester (US-001 AC-5). `principalIdsWithKey(..., 'approval.decide')` leaves out holders of only the scoped entry `approval.decide@fleet.job.shell.escalate`, which is the seeded Developer grant, so a developer who requested the job is not notified of its bash ask. Before this feature the fleet path notified only global admins, so nobody loses a notification they had.

Delete the early-return comment and ASK_KEYS_BY_COMPONENT import. Replace the two suppression unit cases with eligible-delivery cases; retain non-fleet, missing-source, cancelled-source and database-retry regressions. Integration AC-1 and AC-2 enter through the runner relay route and a budget hard stop, never by calling the handler directly. Update the existing relay and budget-notification integrations to assert one engine notification per admin, filtered by kind while the fleet path still exists.

**Scope** — In: engine subscriber and its unit/HTTP notification assertions. Out: deletion of the fleet subscriber/outbox producer belongs to US-002; no requester-based recipient expansion.

**Interface** — `ApprovalRequestedSubscriber.handle`; `decideEligibility(request, principal, keys)`; `NotificationWriter.deliver`. A fleet ask's request gone or no longer pending when handled delivers nothing, preserving existing behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration]: When a bash ask opens pending in project A through the runner relay, every global admin receives one notification of kind approval_request with link /approvals?id=<requestId> and params.key fleet.job.shell.escalate.
AC-2 [integration]: When a budget hard stop opens a pending fleet.budget.override ask in project A, every global admin receives one approval_request notification for that request.
AC-3 [integration]: When a bash ask opens in project A, a user holding the Approver role plus a role granting fleet.job.shell.escalate in A receives its approval_request notification.
AC-4 [integration]: When a bash ask opens in project A, a user holding only the Approver role in A receives no notification for it.
AC-5 [integration]: When a bash ask opens in project A, a project Developer in A holding approval.decide@fleet.job.shell.escalate but not approval.decide receives no notification for it.
AC-6 [integration]: When a bash ask opens in project A, a user holding approval.decide and fleet.job.shell.escalate only in project B receives no notification for it.

AC-7 [unit]: Given a pending payload with permissionKey fleet.job.shell.escalate and one eligible user, ApprovalRequestedSubscriber's handler calls NotificationWriter.deliver once with one draft for that user.

AC-8 [unit]: Given a pending payload with permissionKey fleet.budget.override for a request with projectId null, the handler reads candidates through NotificationEligibility.findGlobalAdminIds and delivers one draft per eligible admin.
AC-9 [unit]: Given a payload with status executed and permissionKey fleet.job.shell.escalate, the handler calls NotificationWriter.deliver zero times.
AC-10 [unit; failure handling]: Given a pending fleet-ask payload whose source request is gone, the handler delivers nothing, preserving the existing missing sources stop quietly behavior.

AC-11 [unit; failure handling]: Given a pending fleet-ask payload whose source request is no longer pending, the handler delivers nothing, preserving the existing ignores sources already cancelled behavior.

userStories.title: Dismiss approval toasts on a successful zero-count refresh
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix #356 by dismissing active approval notices when the current successful counts snapshot is zero.

**Motivation** — The web keeps an approval toast on screen forever once the last pending request is settled elsewhere, on any page that does not receive the project settlement event.

**Approach** — `useApprovalRequestNotifications().refresh` (`apps/web/composables/useApprovalRequestNotifications.ts`)
- Baseline: `if (!snapshot || snapshot.total <= 0 || !userId || !current()) return` before reconciling.
- Target: when the snapshot is non-null with `total <= 0`, the user is signed in and the refresh is current, every active notice is dismissed through `dismiss(id)` and the refresh returns without listing.

The counts snapshot is null (never loaded or failed): The notices stay; #356 must not read a failure as zero.

Reuse dismiss so both the toast id and associated browser Notification are closed. Preserve user/generation/mounted guards and per-user announced history; update the refresh doc comment to describe zero reconciliation. Extend the existing shared-ref Jest harness, retaining its no-list-for-zero case; use a constructible Notification double with close spies for the hidden-tab case.

**Scope** — In: refresh reconciliation and regression tests. Out: web stream/DTO/redirect retirement is US-007; the browser-notification permission prompt and the announce history are unchanged.

**Interface** — `async function refresh(): Promise<void>`; `function dismiss(id: string): void`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit]: Given one shared counts ref, after a refresh with counts { total: 1 } raises a toast for request r1, a refresh with counts { total: 0 } dismisses the toast whose id is r1's toast id.
AC-2 [unit]: When that zero-count refresh runs, it makes no GET /approvals request; the list call count stays at the one from the first refresh.

AC-3 [unit]: Given browser notifications enabled, document.visibilityState hidden and a constructible Notification double whose instances carry a close spy, after r1 raises a browser notification the zero-count refresh calls that instance's close().
AC-4 [unit]: When the counts value is null, refresh leaves the r1 toast undismissed.
AC-5 [unit]: When auth.user is null, a zero-count refresh dismisses nothing through refresh.
AC-6 [unit]: After a zero-count refresh dismisses r1, a later refresh with counts { total: 1 } listing r1 again raises no new toast for r1.

routing.reasoning: One refresh branch reuses existing dismiss and current-user/generation guards; its existing Jest harness supplies all collaborators without a new abstraction.

modifiedFiles.reason: `refresh` dismisses every active notice on a non-null zero-count snapshot before returning; its doc comment says so.
"AC-1: counts total 0 makes no GET /approvals request" keeps its assertion; the new #356 cases are added to this file.

userStories.title: Read engine approvals from the assistant and retire the MCP alias
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Move the assistant list tool onto ApprovalRequestQueries and remove the fleet MCP alias without replacing the engine MCP tool.

**Motivation** — Three adapter routes and a CLI command read the engine through a fleet-shaped DTO, gated by four permission keys nothing else uses.

**Approach** — `koda_list_approvals` (assistant) is gated by `project.read`. It reads `ApprovalRequestQueries.list` for the tool context's actor with `projectId: ctx.projectId`. The engine's visibility already limits rows to the caller's own requests and the ones it may decide, so no approval-specific read key is needed. One line per row: `<id> <permissionKey> <status> <createdAt ISO>`. The status filter is `APPROVAL_REQUEST_STATUSES` (`apps/api/src/approvals/dto/list-approval-requests.query.ts`), default `pending`, in both `parse` and the descriptor. The principal is `{ type: isAgentPrincipal(ctx.actor) ? 'AGENT' : 'USER', id: ctx.actor.id }`, as `action-tools.ts` builds it.

MCP keeps one `koda_list_approvals`: the engine's (`ApprovalMcpTools`). `mcpToolDescriptors()` leaves the assistant descriptor `koda_list_approvals` out instead of renaming it, and `assistantToolName` (the alias map back) is deleted. MCP clients lose `koda_list_fleet_approvals`.

`listApprovalsTool` (`apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/fleet-tools.ts`)
- Baseline: `listApprovalsTool(approvals: ApprovalsService)`, key `fleet.approval.read`.
- Target: `listApprovalsTool(queries: ApprovalRequestQueries)`, key `project.read`; `FleetTools` injects `ApprovalRequestQueries` in place of `ApprovalsService`.

Use engine statuses pending, approved, rejected, expired, cancelled, executed, failed. Keep page size 20, default page 1, no approvals empty output and the existing next-page line. Update descriptor wording to approval requests. Delete ApprovalsService/ApprovalRoute imports and the alias call in mcp-server.factory; MCP names otherwise pass unchanged. Update fleet-tools/origin-tools unit assertions for USER and AGENT principals and project filter, catalog/factory alias cases, and HTTP runner tool plus MCP tools/list integrations.

**Scope** — In: assistant list tool, descriptor, injection, MCP catalog/dispatch alias removal. Out: ApprovalsService/routes are deleted in US-010; a project filter on the engine MCP tool koda_list_approvals is unchanged.

**Interface** — `ApprovalRequestQueries.list(principal: PrincipalRef, filter: ApprovalRequestFilter, page: IPageOption): Promise<IPageResult<ApprovalRequestRecord>>`; `ApprovalRequestFilter` has `status`, `projectId`, `permissionKey`, `jobId`, `mine`. `ApprovalEngineModule` exports `ApprovalRequestQueries`. Integration enters `POST /api/fleet/runner/jobs/:id/tools/koda_list_approvals`, not a direct executor-only surrogate.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration]: In a PROJECT thread of project A, POST /api/fleet/runner/jobs/:id/tools/koda_list_approvals with {} answers one line per pending request of A that the thread's actor may see, each starting with the request id followed by its permissionKey.
AC-2 [integration]: Given a pending request of project B that the same actor may decide, that request does not appear in the project A tool answer.

AC-3 [unit]: listApprovalsTool(queries).execute(ctx, { status: 'pending', page: 2 }) with a user actor calls queries.list once with principal { type: 'USER', id: <the user id> }, filter { status: 'pending', projectId: ctx.projectId } and page { current: 2, size: 20 }.

AC-4 [unit]: listApprovalsTool(queries).execute(ctx, { status: 'pending', page: 2 }) with an agent actor calls queries.list with principal { type: 'AGENT', id: ctx.actor.id }, filter { status: 'pending', projectId: ctx.projectId } and page { current: 2, size: 20 }, matching the user-actor call except for the principal type and id.
AC-5 [unit]: listApprovalsTool(queries).key returns project.read.
AC-6 [unit]: The tool's parse({}) returns { status: 'pending', page: 1 }, and parse({ status: 'executed' }) returns status executed.
AC-7 [unit]: listApprovalsTool(queries).parse({ status: 'decided' }) throws ToolInputError('status'), the invalid-input error the other fleet tools throw for a value outside an enum.
AC-8 [unit]: When queries.list answers an empty page, the tool answers no approvals.
AC-9 [unit]: When queries.list answers a page with hasNext true and current 1, the tool's last line is more: call koda_list_approvals with page 2.
AC-10 [unit]: mcpToolDescriptors() holds no descriptor named koda_list_approvals and none named koda_list_fleet_approvals.
AC-11 [integration]: An MCP tools/list call through POST /api/mcp answers exactly one tool named koda_list_approvals, whose description is the ApprovalMcpTools one.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Stop sending fleet.approval.requested/resolved, leaving the engine webhook family as the only approval webhook output.

**Motivation** — Every fleet ask sends `fleet.approval.*` beside the engine's `approval.requested`/`approval.resolved` (7a).

Recorder counts follow the engine: one approval.resolved per non-pending status the engine records. A subscription listing only the old requested event receives no delivery. userStories.title: Delete API fleet approval live events and publication markers
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Remove fleet_approval live publication and its persisted acknowledgement while preserving engine events and once-only fleet activity.

**Motivation** — Every fleet ask change publishes `fleet_approval` beside the engine's `approval_request`, threaded through about fifteen fleet files.

**Approach** — `FleetApprovalAsk.publishedStatus` is dropped (US-006, migration `20261110090000_fleet_ask_drop_published_status`). It only acknowledged `fleet_approval` frames. `recordedStatus` stays: it keeps the activity row once-only.

`ApprovalChange.live` goes, and the closer stops answering frames. `closeForJob` and `recordResolved` answer `Promise<void>`; `JobTransitionsService.apply` loses `approvalLive`; `CommandAckProcessor.process` and `JobReportProcessor` lose their `approvalLive` lists.

Deletion only:
- `ApprovalLivePublisher` and its spec, `LiveFleetApprovalEvent` and its member of the `LiveEvent` union;
- `ApprovalChange.live`, every `approvalLive` list, field and publish call in jobs, sync, budgets and the two approval sweepers;
- the publication half of `FleetAskEventsSubscriber` (`liveFrameId`, the `publish` flag, `setPublishedStatus`), the store and repository `setPublishedStatus`, and the domain field `publishedStatus`;
- the column `FleetApprovalAsk.publishedStatus` (schema plus migration `20261110090000_fleet_ask_drop_published_status`).

`ApprovalCloser`: after US-002 the constructor has no outbox; after US-005 no webhooks; after US-006 it is `(store, askService, activity, audit)`, `ApprovalChange` is `{ approval, answer? }`, and `closeForJob` and `recordResolved` answer `Promise<void>`. FleetAskEventsSubscriber.record returns nothing and runs only when recordedStatus differs; keep link locking, marker/activity atomicity and actor attribution. Preserve bounded job/policy close algorithms, held-request skipping, persisted first-close intent, runner APPROVAL_ANSWER and existing job live/wakeup committed effects.

`ApprovalRequestLiveSubscriber` (`apps/api/src/live/approval-request-live.subscriber.ts`) publishes `approval_request` for every `APPROVAL_REQUEST_CHANGED` with a project; it becomes the only approval live event.

Remove publisher DI registration/exports and update all affected constructor doubles/return shapes, including job transitions, command ack/report/sync/sweeper, budget evaluator/sweeper/service/command and both close sweepers. Replace frame-count assertions in bounded-close tests with engine close calls; preserve rollback and activity/recordedStatus assertions in recorder/repository/job-end integrations. Delete only old publication retry/acknowledgement tests.

**Scope** — In: API live plumbing, persisted publication marker, schema migration and dependent tests. Out: web handler removal is US-007; adapter routes are US-010; FleetApprovalAsk.recordedStatus and fleet activity rows remain unchanged; no replacement fleet live event.

**Interface** — `ApprovalChange` is `{ approval, answer? }`; `closeForJob` and `recordResolved` answer `Promise<void>`. Removals are verified by the build/static gate: `bun run type-check` and `bun run lint` in `apps/api`.

**Goal** — Let the unified approval CLI express the decisions currently available only through the fleet command.

**Motivation** — Three adapter routes and a CLI command read the engine through a fleet-shaped DTO, gated by four permission keys nothing else uses.

**Approach** — The CLI gains decision params before the fleet command goes (US-011). `koda fleet approval decide` is today the only CLI path that can approve a budget ask (the engine requires `params.amountUsd`) or answer `allow_for_job`. `koda approval approve` gains `--choice <allow|allow_for_job>`, `--amount <usd>` and `--requeue <all|ids>`, sent as the decide body's `params`. `--amount` is sent as a JSON number (the budget command's `isRaiseAmount` refuses a string), validated with the rule of `parseBudgetUsd` (`apps/cli/src/utils/parse-usd.ts`: more than 0, at most 1,000,000, at most 4 decimals). `--requeue all` reads `details.requeueCandidates` from `GET /approvals/:id` and refuses when `details.requeueCandidatesTruncated` is true. Every option check runs inside the action, not as a Commander option parser: a failed check calls `handleApiError(err, { validationError: true })` (exit 3) and returns, as `approval policy set` does, so no decide request follows under the spec harness's no-op `process.exit`.

`registerDecision` (`apps/cli/src/commands/approval.ts`)
- Baseline: `approve <id>` and `reject <id>` take `--comment` and `--json`.
- Target: `approve <id>` also takes `--choice`, `--amount` and `--requeue`.

Refuse requeue all if details has no requeueCandidates, including null details; truncated candidates must print a stderr message naming koda approval show <id>. Explicit ids are split on commas and sent unchanged; only all needs the GET. Keep existing approve/reject behavior, comments and JSON output. Without any new option omit params entirely. Normal API failures still use the existing error handler behavior.

**Scope** — In: unified approve options and generated-boundary command tests. Out: deleting fleet CLI/client is US-012. The CLI does not read request keys to reject bash/budget option mismatches; the API answers 400. Duplicate ids, empty entries, whitespace, all mixed with ids and server candidate limits remain API-owned. --choice deny on approve remains invalid; use koda approval reject.

**Interface** — `approvalRequestsControllerGet` and `approvalRequestsControllerDecide` (`apps/cli/src/generated/sdk.gen.ts`); the decide body already has `params?: Record<string, unknown>`. `params` is `{ choice }` or `{ amountUsd, requeueJobIds? }`.

**Goal** — Remove obsolete fleet.approval permission keys without invalidating stored roles or leaving unexecutable legacy requests pending.

**Motivation** — Three adapter routes and a CLI command read the engine through a fleet-shaped DTO, gated by four permission keys nothing else uses.

**Approach** — The key migration (US-013, `20261111090000_retire_fleet_approval_keys`):
- strips every entry containing the text `fleet.approval.` (exact keys, `.*` patterns, negations and `approval.decide@fleet.approval.*` scopes) from every `Role.permissions`. It must run before the new code serves: the unlocked `developer` system role still stores `fleet.approval.decide.bash`, the seeder never rewrites an unlocked role, and `PermissionService` drops a whole role (logging `invalid permission entry`) when one stored entry names a key the catalog no longer has;
- deletes `ApprovalPolicy` rows whose `permissionPattern` starts with `fleet.approval.`;
- sets `status = 'cancelled'` and `settledAt = NOW()` on `ApprovalRequest` rows whose `permissionKey` starts with `fleet.approval.` and whose status is `pending` or `approved` (their route commands no longer exist, so they can never execute);
- rewrites `Notification.link` `/admin/fleet/approvals` to `/approvals` (the redirect pages are deleted in US-007).
- The SQL holds no literal `;` inside a statement and no `DO $$` block (the migration test helper `migrationStatements` splits on `;`); the role rewrite is `COALESCE((SELECT jsonb_agg(e ORDER BY ord) FROM jsonb_array_elements("permissions") WITH ORDINALITY AS t(e, ord) WHERE position('fleet.approval.' in e #>> '{}') = 0), '[]'::jsonb)`, so the remaining entries keep their order and a role left with none stores `[]`, never NULL. Its test seeds pre-migration rows with `scratchSchemaBefore(url, schema, '20261111090000_retire_fleet_approval_keys')`, as `developer-bash-decide-migration.integration.spec.ts` does.

The inventory TSV follows the catalog (US-013). `catalog.spec.ts` asserts the catalog equals the keys of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-action-inventory.tsv` plus the new-key list, so the TSV loses the seven `fleet/approvals` route rows and its `koda_list_approvals` row is re-keyed to `project.read`.

**Scope** — In: catalog/seed/inventory/snapshot changes and stored role/policy/request/notification migration. Out: route deletion is US-010; redirect deletion is US-007. **Interface** — migration `20261111090000_retire_fleet_approval_keys`; `PERMISSION_CATALOG`; `SYSTEM_ROLES`; `scratchSchemaBefore(url, schema, '20261111090000_retire_fleet_approval_keys')`.
